title: Scaffolding
summary: Temporary timber frameworks give builders access to elevated work and materials.

parents.reason: Shaped timber members supplied the poles and platforms from which early scaffolds were built.

title: Falsework
summary: Temporary supports hold arches, concrete forms, and other structures until they can carry their own loads.

parents.reason: Assembled timber members formed temporary load-bearing frames used in ancient bridge and viaduct work.

title: Concrete formwork
summary: Temporary or reusable molds shape concrete before it hardens into structural members.

parents.reason: Concrete's moldable wet state allowed builders to cast slabs, vaults, and domes in shaped forms.
Falsework supports shuttering molds while fresh concrete is placed and gains strength.

title: Slipform construction
summary: Moving or incrementally raised forms cast continuous concrete structures without separate construction joints.

parents.reason: Concrete's controlled workability and setting let a moving form leave material that could support itself.
parents.directContribution: Slipforming depends on freshly placed concrete gaining enough early strength to support the advancing form; this material behavior controls the process rate and feasibility, beyond concrete's general role as a moldable material.

parents.reason: Slipforming advances or raises concrete molds continuously instead of placing discrete stationary forms.

title: Building information modeling
summary: BIM's concept emerged in the 1970s as digital building representations began linking geometry with functional data for design, construction, and operation; software implementations appeared from the late 1970s into the early 1980s.

parents.reason: Computer systems made it possible to create, store, and exchange information-rich digital building models.

title: Land surveying
summary: Surveyors determine terrestrial positions and boundaries from measured distances and angles for maps, property, and construction.

title: Triangulation surveying
summary: Measured angles in linked triangles establish distant positions and large-area maps without measuring every baseline directly.

parents.reason: Geometric relations convert measured triangle angles and a known baseline into estimated distances.

title: Theodolite
summary: Jonathan Sisson's 1725 instrument combined a sighting telescope, horizontal and vertical axes, and graduated scales to read both angle directions.

title: Gunter's chain surveying
summary: A 66-foot chain divided into 100 links made land distances and areas easier to measure and calculate consistently.

parents.reason: Chain measurements let surveyors record parcel boundaries and plot land from field distances.
The fixed chain and link lengths reconciled customary land units with decimal calculations of acreage.

title: Roman cadastral survey
summary: A Roman land survey recorded state parcel boundaries in Campania in AD 77, supporting recovery of public land and renewed taxation.

parents.reason: Measured and mapped parcel boundaries made land records geographically specific.
Land surveys identified state holdings and taxable property for reassessment and collection.

title: Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing
summary: A symbolic drawing language specifies the allowed variation in a part's size, shape, orientation, and feature location.

parents.reason: Interchangeable production required explicit limits describing which dimensional and geometric variations still permit parts to fit.

title: Coordinate-measuring machine
summary: Ferranti's early two-axis coordinate-measuring machine used a probe and coordinate readings to measure precision military components.

title: Palletized unit loads
summary: A flat reusable platform groups goods into stable loads that can be lifted, stored, and moved together.

parents.reason: Forklift forks lift and move the stable platform together with its grouped goods.

title: Barcode identification
summary: Machine-readable bar patterns identify goods or vehicles for automatic recording and tracking.

parents.reason: Woodland and Silver adapted Morse code's short and long marks into narrow and wide bars for machine-readable product identification.

title: Heathrow LACES cargo-data interchange
summary: London Airport Cargo EDP Scheme (LACES), introduced at Heathrow in 1971, let forwarding agents enter cargo data into customs processing and reduced clearance time.

parents.reason: Electronic computers processed structured cargo and customs records automatically.

title: Just-in-time inventory control
summary: Production draws and replenishes materials in response to actual demand, reducing stocks held between operations.

parents.reason: The practice reorganized replenishment and in-process stock so materials arrived as actual production demand required them.

title: Supply-chain management
summary: Organizations coordinate sourcing, production, logistics, information, and delivery across suppliers and customers.

parents.reason: Supply-chain management explicitly integrates the storage and transport of goods into wider sourcing, production, and demand plans.
parents.directContribution: Logistics remains a direct component of supply-chain management across storage, movement, and delivery; freight forwarding covers only shipment arrangement and does not account for the integrated sourcing, production, and demand functions.

parents.reason: Electronic exchange of structured business and shipping documents supports the information flows coordinated across supply-chain partners.

title: Universal Product Code retail scanning
summary: Retail scanners read standardized UPC labels to identify products automatically at checkout.

parents.reason: UPC retail scanning applied machine-readable barcodes to standardized product identification at checkout.

title: Spirit level
summary: Attested in Thevenot's 1661 correspondence, a liquid-filled glass vial with an air bubble indicated whether a surface was level.

parents.reason: Glass formed the transparent, slightly curved vial that contained the liquid and made the leveling bubble visible.
